name: ansible-flow-designer
description: Visual, top-down designer for Ansible automation flows: sketch typed nodes and ports, run a walking skeleton, then bind nodes to modules, roles and playbooks.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode you can design and edit flows and generate playbooks. Runs, the Ansible probe (module catalog, lenses, code sync) and the environment and AWX address settings of the workspace need a trusted workspace.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Design Ansible automation as a diagram, then run it as a playbook. Flows are files in a folder: open one to begin (an empty folder is fine).
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
New here? [Get Started](command:afd.help.getStarted)

No flows in this folder yet.
[New Flow](command:afd.flow.new)
[Open Sample Flow](command:afd.help.openSample)
Already have playbooks? [Import Ansible Playbooks](command:afd.import.playbooks)
New here? [Get Started](command:afd.help.getStarted) · [User Guide](command:afd.help.openGuide)

afd.codegen.onSave.markdownDescription: Write generated code to `generated/` next to the flow whenever a flow without errors is saved. Files edited by hand are never overwritten without asking.

afd.canvas.direction.markdownDescription: Direction of the automatic layout: where nodes without a stored position appear, and how **Tidy Up** lays out a level. A setting of yours, never written to the flow file.

afd.environment.kind.markdownDescription: Where Ansible runs. `auto`: a container when an image is set (here or in the Red Hat Ansible extension's execution environment settings), else a local interpreter (VS Code Remote, venv). Native Windows needs a container.

afd.environment.image.markdownDescription: Execution environment image for the probe and runs, e.g. `registry.example.net/ee/netops:2.19`. Empty: use `ansible.executionEnvironment.image` when the Red Hat Ansible extension enables execution environments.

afd.environment.containerEngine.description: Container engine for the image (auto: the Red Hat Ansible setting, else docker).

afd.environment.containerOptions.markdownDescription: Extra `docker run` / `podman run` arguments, one per item (e.g. `-v`, `~/.ssh:/home/ansible/.ssh:ro` for keys).

afd.environment.python.markdownDescription: Python with ansible-core 2.19+ for local mode. Empty: `ansible.python.interpreterPath`, else `python3`.

afd.run.inventory.markdownDescription: Inventory for runs, relative to the repository root. Empty: the default from `ansible.cfg`.

afd.run.askVaultPassword.markdownDescription: Ask for the vault password before a run (`auto`: when the inventory or repository vars contain vault data). The password is used for that run only and never stored.

afd.runs.keep.markdownDescription: Run folders kept per flow in the extension storage (their event logs). Older ones are deleted when a run starts. Run inputs are never kept: secret-looking ones never reach the disk and the rest are deleted when the run ends.

afd.awx.url.markdownDescription: AWX address for _Launch in AWX_, e.g. `https://awx.example.net`. The token is kept in VS Code's secret storage (_Set AWX Token_), never in settings.

afd.awx.verifyTls.markdownDescription: Verify AWX's TLS certificate. Turn off only for a lab AWX with a self-signed certificate.

languageModelTools.name: afd_flow_describe
languageModelTools.userDescription: Describe an Ansible flow by key: nodes, wires, subflows, open fail ports, problem counts and the revision to pass to flow_edit. Read this before editing.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Describe an Ansible flow by key: nodes, wires, subflows, open fail ports, problem counts and the revision to pass to flow_edit. Read this before editing. Ansible Flow Designer flows (*.flow.yaml); see the ansible-flow skill.

path.description: The flow file (*.flow.yaml), relative to the workspace root. Default: the flow open in the designer, or the only flow.

level.description: all (default), top, or a subflow key to describe one level.

layout.description: Also list where each node is ("at x,y" for a stored position, "auto x,y" where the canvas places it now) and run the layout check: what a person sees on the canvas that you cannot, per level (boxes overlapping, a wire through a box, a wire label on a box or another label, wires crossing). Use it before move, to place new nodes next to existing ones, and after building a flow. flow_edit runs the same check on the levels it placed nodes on.

languageModelTools.name: afd_flow_edit

languageModelTools.modelDescription: Edit an Ansible flow with ops that name nodes by key (never IDs). The ops run in order, all or nothing; nodes added earlier in the batch can be used by later ops. Returns what changed, new problems and the new revision. Ansible Flow Designer flows (*.flow.yaml); see the ansible-flow skill.

ops.description: Ops in order; flow_reference topic ops lists them with examples.

anyOf.description: Add a node. after continues from an output port: a free port is wired to the new node, a wired one gets the node on its wire (so a chain grows: a new flow is start -> done). on_wire does the same for a wired port only, failed_to wires its failed_hosts. The key comes from the title unless given. Use in to add it inside a subflow.

type.description: start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).

title.description: Human name shown on the canvas.

key.description: Key of the new node; default: from the title. Must be new on its level.

in.description: Subflow whose inner level gets the node (default: top).

after.description: Continue from this output port: wired to the new node, or the node goes on its wire when the port is wired already.

on_wire.description: Put the new node on the wire leaving this output port (between both ends).

failed_to.description: Wire the new node's failed_hosts to this node.

intent.description: What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.

items.description: A port name. Which ports a node has depends on its type: see the port catalog. Parallel branch ports are branch_1, branch_2, ...

ports.description: Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).

purpose.description: Format 2: what the node is for in failure handling (rollback, notify, retry, exclude); the patterns set it, and a Rollback is found by it.

condition.description: Decision nodes: Jinja expression evaluated per host.

branches.description: Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)

join_mode.description: Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one

type.description: Value type. host_list is a list of inventory hosts or groups.

required.description: Inputs: a run must provide a value.

default.description: Inputs: value used when none is given.

from.description: Where the value comes from: <node_key>.<output> (an earlier node's output, on this level or around it), flow.<input> (a flow input), <subflow_key>.<input> inside that subflow (its input), or impl.register[.path] (outputs: the bound task's registered result). A subflow's outputs name an inner step's output (<step>.<output>); without from, the inner output of the same name.

targets.description: Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

inputs.description: Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.

A subflow's outputs name an inner step's output (<step>.<output>); without from, the inner output of the same name.

targets.description: Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

outputs.description: Values the node produces for later nodes.

max_fail_percentage.description: Fail the whole node when more than this share of hosts fail.

serial.description: Batch size or percentage for rolling execution.

rolling.description: Subflows: hosts per batch (a number, or a percentage like 25%) through every step inside, one batch after another. The steps run in one play with this serial; a step that needs plays of its own (a subflow, approval, parallel, join, playbook binding, inventory_target, or its own serial or max_fail_percentage) stops it (rolling-unsupported).

timeout.description: Task timeout, e.g. 300 or 5m. Hosts that time out leave through the timeout port.

retries.description: Retries before a host fails (module steps). Without until, a step stops retrying on its first success.

delay.description: Seconds between retries (Ansible delay, default 5). retries x delay is how long a step polls.

until.description: Poll until this holds: a Jinja test without braces, e.g. wait_ha_result.json.results | length == 2. It reads the step's registered result (impl.register, else <key with _ for ->_result) and its inputs. Module steps only; retries sets the attempts.

become.description: Run with privilege escalation. Format 2: set on a subflow, it applies to the steps inside (the nearest setting wins).

become_user.description: Format 2: whom to become (Ansible become_user); set on a subflow, it applies inside. Format 1 writes it as a task keyword.

inventory_target.description: Run the node's work on this host pattern instead of the arriving hosts (they leave together afterwards).

tags.description: Extra Ansible tags for the generated play.

ref.description: Fully qualified module or role name (e.g. ansible.builtin.ping, netops.baseline), or the playbook path in the repository.

collection_version.description: Collection version the binding was made against.

params.description: Module parameters or role variables. Jinja may reference inputs by name.

register.description: Variable that keeps the task result; outputs read it with from: impl.register.

keywords.description: Ansible task keywords written on the generated task as they are (module and role bindings). Jinja may reference inputs by name; when, changed_when and failed_when are Jinja tests without braces. What the flow models itself is set there instead: register (impl.register), tags, become, timeout, retries, delay and until (settings), handlers (steps with when: <register> is changed), block and rescue (subflows and failure paths).

when.description: Jinja test without braces (or a list, all must hold): hosts for which it is false skip the task and leave through ok_hosts.

changed_when.description: Jinja test without braces that decides whether the result counts as changed; may read the registered result.

failed_when.description: Jinja test without braces that decides whether the task failed; may read the registered result.

loop.description: List to run the task over, usually Jinja ("{{ interfaces }}"); each item is item (or loop_control.loop_var).

loop_control.description: Loop options: loop_var, index_var, label, pause, extended.

ignore_errors.description: true: a failure is ignored and the host leaves through ok_hosts instead of failed_hosts.

delegate_to.description: Run the task on this host instead (e.g. localhost), on behalf of each arriving host.

delegate_facts.description: With delegate_to: facts go to the delegated host.

run_once.description: Run the task once for the batch, on the first host; the result applies to every host.

no_log.description: Hide the task result in the log (use for secrets).

check_mode.description: true: always run in check mode; false: run for real even in check mode.

diff.description: Show or hide the diff of changes for this task.

environment.description: Environment variables for the task (a map, or Jinja).

become_flags.description: Extra flags for the become method.

connection.description: Connection plugin for this task (local, network_cli, ...).

throttle.description: Most hosts running this task at the same time.

async.description: Run in the background for at most this many seconds.

poll.description: Seconds between status checks of an async task (0: do not wait).

vars.description: Task variables; for a role binding, put role variables in params instead.

module_defaults.description: Default parameters for modules run by this task.

debugger.description: When to start the task debugger (always, never, on_failed, ...).

^with_[a-z_]+$.description: A with_<lookup> loop (with_items, with_dict, ...): prefer loop.

impl.description: What the node runs: a module, a role or a playbook. Absent: a TODO stub.

position.description: Where the new node goes; leave it out for automatic placement. Where the node goes: {x, y}, or exactly one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of the same level (key, or subflow/step), with an optional gap in pixels (default 56 below/above, 48 beside); a relative place steps aside until it is free. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

delegate_facts.description: With delegate_to: facts go to the delegated host.

run_once.description: Run the task once for the batch, on the first host; the result applies to every host.

no_log.description: Hide the task result in the log (use for secrets).

check_mode.description: true: always run in check mode; false: run for real even in check mode.

diff.description: Show or hide the diff of changes for this task.

environment.description: Environment variables for the task (a map, or Jinja).

become_flags.description: Extra flags for the become method.

connection.description: Connection plugin for this task (local, network_cli, ...).

throttle.description: Most hosts running this task at the same time.

async.description: Run in the background for at most this many seconds.

poll.description: Seconds between status checks of an async task (0: do not wait).

vars.description: Task variables; for a role binding, put role variables in params instead.

module_defaults.description: Default parameters for modules run by this task.

debugger.description: When to start the task debugger (always, never, on_failed, ...).

^with_[a-z_]+$.description: A with_<lookup> loop (with_items, with_dict, ...): prefer loop.

anyOf.description: Place or move nodes and annotations (positions only; nothing else changes). Several in one op, in order: a later one may be placed relative to an earlier one. A section carries the nodes and annotations wholly inside it; a note on a node moves with the node. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

nodes.description: Node (key, or subflow/step) -> where it goes.

additionalProperties.description: Where the node goes: {x, y}, or exactly one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of the same level (key, or subflow/step), with an optional gap in pixels (default 56 below/above, 48 beside); a relative place steps aside until it is free. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

left_of.description: Left of this node, level with it.

A note on a node (on) moves with the node, is deleted with it, and its text becomes a comment above the node's code. A section is a titled region behind nodes: moving it moves what is inside. Text is words with no background. The text is Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, - lists, [links](https://...).

languageModelTools.name: afd_flow_new
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a new Ansible flow diagram: a *.flow.yaml file that Ansible Flow Designer draws and turns into playbooks. Use it whenever the user asks for an Ansible flow, flow diagram or automation flow, instead of drawing one in PlantUML, Mermaid or draw.io. The flow starts as start -> done with a devices host_list input; then add steps with flow_edit (add_node after start.ok_hosts puts the first step between them).

The flow starts as start -> done with a devices host_list input; then add steps with flow_edit (add_node after start.ok_hosts puts the first step between them). walkthroughs.title: Design your first Ansible flow
walkthroughs.description: Start a flow, add a step, see the playbook it makes, decide what happens when it fails, and run it as a skeleton.

steps.title: Start a flow
steps.description:
A flow is a diagram of steps that becomes a playbook, kept as YAML (`*.flow.yaml`) next to your playbooks. Start a new one, or copy a sample into this folder.
[New Flow](command:afd.flow.new)
[Open Sample Flow](command:afd.help.openSample)
Already have playbooks? [Import Ansible Playbooks](command:afd.import.playbooks) · Tip: an empty folder is fine. [Tutorial: your first flow](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F01-first-flow.md%22%5D)

media.altText: A firewall upgrade flow on the designer canvas

steps.title: Add a step
steps.description:
**Add a Step** (or N) puts a step between Start and Done; N again adds the next one after it. Wires run from a port to the next step: hosts that succeed leave by `ok_hosts`, those that fail by `failed_hosts`.
[How-to: canvas basics](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fcanvas-basics.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Quick add inserting a task on a wire

steps.title: See the playbook it makes
steps.description:
Each step becomes a play in `generated/<key>.yml`, written when you save. Select a step and choose **Peek Code** to see its play.
[Generate Code](command:afd.code.generate)
[How-to: code generation](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fcode-generation.md%22%5D)

media.altText: A node selected, with its Details on the right

steps.title: Decide what happens when it fails
steps.description:
An amber port is a failure nothing handles yet: its hosts would fail the run. The banner asks what should happen; pick a pattern (rollback, notify and stop, exclude and report, retry) in one click, or keep it open with **Accept with Reason…**.
[How-to: ports and failure patterns](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fports-and-failure-patterns.md%22%5D)

media.altText: The port menu of an open failed_hosts port

steps.title: Run it as a skeleton
steps.description:
Steps without code print TODO, so the flow runs from the first minute: `ansible-playbook --check` in your Ansible environment. No environment yet? [Set Up Ansible Environment…](command:afd.environment.setup). Run mode then shows how many hosts took each wire.
[Run as Skeleton](command:afd.run.skeleton)
[How-to: runs and environments](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fruns-and-environments.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Run mode with host counts on every wire

steps.title: Keep going
steps.description:
Split the flow into subflows (top-down), bind steps to modules from your environment's catalog, pass data between them, and run for real or in AWX.
[Open the User Guide](command:afd.help.openGuide)
[Tutorial: from design to production](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F02-design-to-production.md%22%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Build flows with an AI assistant
walkthroughs.description: Copilot, Claude Code, Codex and other agents learn the flow format and edit flows by key with the flow tools.

steps.title: Copilot is ready
steps.description:
In Copilot's agent mode the `ansible-flow` skill and ten flow tools are there without setup. Ask for a flow, or for a change to the open one.
[Open Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

steps.title: Set up Claude Code, Codex and other agents
steps.description:
Agents in a terminal or another editor need the skill copied and the flow tools registered once. The extension offers it when it finds them; you can also run it any time.
[Set Up AI Assistants](command:afd.ai.setup)
[How-to: AI assistants](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fai-assistants.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Ask for a flow
steps.description:
Say what the automation should achieve, how it is split into phases and what happens to failed hosts. The agent builds the flow with all-or-nothing edits and fixes the problems it causes.
[Tutorial: build a flow with an AI assistant](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F04-ai-assistant.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Import playbooks with an assistant
steps.description:
Turn existing playbooks into a flow designed by intent: **Import Ansible Playbooks…** → **With an AI assistant**. Copilot Chat opens with the prompt ready; other assistants get it on the clipboard.
[Import Ansible Playbooks](command:afd.import.playbooks)
[Tutorial: bring existing playbooks into flows](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F05-import-playbooks.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Review and fix
steps.description:
The canvas shows every edit. Check the Problems panel, and ask the agent to fix what is left without changing the logic.
[Check Flow](command:afd.flow.check)

walkthroughs.title: Run your flows in AWX
walkthroughs.description: Turn a flow into an AWX job template or approval workflow, launch it from VS Code and follow it on the canvas.

steps.title: Connect to AWX
steps.description:
Point the extension at your AWX and store a personal access token in VS Code's secret storage.
[Open the AWX setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22afd.awx.url%22%5D)
[Set AWX Token](command:afd.awx.setToken)

steps.title: Set up the template
steps.description:
Create the job template (or the approval workflow) for the open flow, in the AWX project that holds your repository.
[Set Up AWX Template](command:afd.awx.setupTemplate)
[How-to: AWX](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fawx.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Approvals become AWX approvals
steps.description:
Top-level approval nodes split the flow into a workflow with an approval node at each gate. Local runs approve by themselves, or take the outcome you pass in `afd_approvals`.
[How-to: approvals](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fapprovals.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Launch and follow the run
steps.description:
Launch asks for the flow inputs and confirms the targets and the commit. Run mode shows every node's hosts, failures and times, and offers to mark nodes tested after a passing run.
[Launch in AWX](command:afd.awx.launch)
[Tutorial: AWX end to end](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F03-awx-end-to-end.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Run mode replaying an AWX job

steps.title: Import an existing AWX workflow or job template
steps.description:
Turn a workflow or job template you already have into a flow, from AWX or from an `awx export` file. Playbooks of this repository become steps.
[Import AWX Workflow or Job Template](command:afd.import.awx)
[How-to: import playbooks and AWX templates](command:afd.help.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fimport.md%22%5D)

media.altText: A flow imported from an AWX workflow
